definition: Sporadic means occurring at irregular, scattered intervals.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sporadic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sporadic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Sales of the board game are sporadic: the shop can go a month without selling one, then wrap three before lunch.
Occasional says only that a thing happens now and then; sporadic adds the jolt of irregularity — clusters, droughts, no telling which.
Patternless goes past sporadic — not merely scattered in time, but with no logic left for even the patientest observer to find.

Scattered is the root picture behind sporadic: things strewn thinly about, like seed flung across a field. It can cover space or time, but it reports only the thin spread. Sporadic sharpens the claim about timing — events at irregular intervals, in clusters and droughts, with no telling when the next comes.

Patchy describes uneven coverage — fog patchy over the valley, a lawn gone patchy after a dry August. The gaps sit in fixed places you could point to. Sporadic is about time instead: events arriving at irregular, scattered intervals that no clock will pin down.

Where the gaps are regular — every ten seconds, every third day — the precise word is periodic.

Rain in the basin is sporadic, and everything alive there is built around that fact.
A storm may soak one arroyo three times in a week, then skip the whole valley for fourteen months.
The wildflowers cannot afford a calendar.
Their seeds wait in the gravel — a year, a decade — for the one wet night that tells them to go.
Ranchers keep rain logs going back to their grandparents, hoping to find a rhythm.
The logs show streaks and silences, and no rhythm at all.
Visitors from wetter places always ask when the rainy season starts.
The oldest rancher likes to answer: it doesn't start; it ambushes.
